solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, linked answer split by the grid); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Army chap hurt but help may be at hand

indicators.note: something hurt is damaged or knocked out of shape, so the letters of the two words are reshuffled

explanation.surface: A soldier has been injured, but assistance is nearby.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hurt' rearranges the eight letters of ARMY CHAP. The definition is a descriptive phrase: a chemist's shop is where help for ailments is close by.
explanation.definitionFit: A chemist's shop is a place where remedies and advice are readily available, a cryptic description.

clue.text: Said group has suggestion for Indian food

indicators.note: said means spoken, so the words are judged by how they sound rather than spelt

parts.note: a group is a pack, and a suggestion or hint of something is an aura; together they are spoken

explanation.surface: A spokesperson reports that a committee has an idea about what curry to order.
explanation.walkthrough: Spoken quickly, PACK plus AURA (a faint hint of something) runs together as the fried snack's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A pakora is a deep-fried battered snack from South Asian cookery, an example of the dishes meant.

clue.text: Got up in Paris, enlivened

indicators.note: in tells us the letters sit inside the words that follow, running across the comma

explanation.surface: Someone rose from bed in the French capital feeling refreshed.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean having risen from sitting or lying, a straight synonym in the past participle.

clue.text: Throwing up proposal to disgusted head

parts.note: a proposal put to a meeting is a motion
disgusted means sick, as in 'sick of it'
a ness is a headland, a head jutting into the sea

explanation.surface: A sickened person heaves at a suggestion put to their boss.
explanation.walkthrough: Head here is a promontory, as in place names like Loch Ness's neighbours Sheerness and Dungeness.
explanation.definitionFit: Travel nausea is the condition that leads to vomiting on boats and cars, so the phrase describes being ill.

clue.text: Question — "aren't I able to use force?" — needs support

parts.note: aren't I able is can't I
to lever is to use force to prise something with a bar

explanation.surface: Someone frustrated asks whether they may push hard, needing something to hold up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Question' just tells us the quoted words form a question, CAN'T I LEVER?
explanation.definitionFit: A cantilever is a projecting beam that holds up a structure, a type of bracing.

clue.text: Put paid to time out, assuming river will dry up

indicators.note: assuming means taking on, so the shortened word takes in the letter
out says this letter is dropped from the word

parts.note: to scotch something is to put paid to it, to end it

explanation.surface: Ending a period of time out will make a river run dry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' removes T from SCOTCH to give SCOCH, and 'assuming' puts R inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To scorch is to parch with heat, so it is a synonym of drying something out.

clue.text: The dog on the track is mine

parts.note: a collie is a breed of sheepdog
RY is short for railway, a track

explanation.surface: A dog standing on the railway line is claimed as one's own.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mine' looks like a possessive but is the noun, a coal pit.
explanation.definitionFit: A colliery is a coal pit with its buildings, a kind of underground excavation.

clue.text: One may herald the approach of cats and dogs!

definitions.text: One may herald the approach of cats and dogs!

parts.words: One may herald the approach of cats and dogs!
parts.note: it raining cats and dogs is a heavy downpour, and a first drop of water announces it is coming

explanation.surface: Something signals that pets are on their way.
explanation.definitionFit: A single falling drop of water warns that a heavy downpour is about to start.

clue.text: Moved home, for example, to US state dominance

indicators.note: moved means shifted about, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: NY is the abbreviation for New York

explanation.surface: Someone relocated house, for instance to an American state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Moved' looks like part of the house-moving story but signals the rearrangement of the first two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Hegemony is leadership or control by one state over others, a synonym for supremacy.

clue.text: Coming together for handicraft

definitions.meaning: broken bones are said to knit when they join and heal
a craft of making fabric with needles and yarn

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both joining up, as healing bones do, and the needlework craft with wool.

clue.text: Hurried defence of airborne transport

parts.note: flying means rushing, hurrying along
a fortress is a stronghold, a defence

explanation.surface: A hastily built defensive system for aircraft.
explanation.definitionFit: The Boeing B-17 bomber of the Second World War carried that name, an aircraft example.

clue.text: Eloquence of mutinous choirmasters missing Mass

indicators.note: mutinous suggests rebellion and disorder, so the letters are rearranged
missing tells us the letters of the word Mass are taken out of the pool

explanation.surface: Rebellious choir leaders speak persuasively but skip church service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missing' takes M, A, S, S out of CHOIRMASTERS, leaving CHOIRTER, which 'mutinous' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhetoric is the art of persuasive speaking, so it stands for fluent, effective language.

clue.text: Prudence and Norman

definitions.meaning: prudence is sound judgement and good sense
Norman ... was a popular British slapstick film comedian

explanation.walkthrough: Both definitions read like first names; the second is the surname of comedian Norman Wisdom.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means sound judgement, and it is the surname of the British comic actor Norman.

clue.text: CIA slips me new material on my pet subject

indicators.note: new means made afresh, so the letters are formed into a different word

explanation.surface: An intelligence agency leaks fresh documents about a favourite topic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges CIA SLIPS ME; 'material on' just links the anagram to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A specialism is an area of expertise, the field someone knows best and enjoys.

clue.text: Attack on old-fashioned stuff of little value

parts.note: to pepper is to attack with a hail of shots
corn is sentimental or dated material, as in corny

explanation.surface: An assault on outdated material that is worth very little.
explanation.walkthrough: A peppercorn rent is a nominal one, hence the adjective-like sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A peppercorn sum is a token payment, so the word describes something nominal and trivial.

clue.text: Determined to encourage journalist

parts.note: to spirit, or spirit up, is to animate and encourage
ED is short for editor, a journalist

explanation.surface: Resolved to give a reporter some support.
explanation.definitionFit: Spirited means full of courage and resolve, a near synonym for a resolute attitude.

clue.text: See 10
See 3
Foresight of US vice-president welcoming first Roman poet

indicators.note: welcoming means taking in, so the name holds the other letters

parts.note: Mike Pence was US vice-president from 2017 to 2021

indicators.note: first picks the opening letter of the word Roman

parts.note: Ovid was a Latin poet of ancient Rome

explanation.surface: An American politician shows good judgement by hosting an early Roman writer.
explanation.definitionFit: Providence means prudent forethought and care for the future, a synonym of foresight.

clue.text: Reported excessively offensive dealer

indicators.note: reported means spoken of, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: gross means offensive, so more gross is grosser

explanation.surface: Word is that a trader was extremely rude.
explanation.definitionFit: A grocer is a shopkeeper selling food, a kind of trader or merchant.

clue.text: Imagined being over the moon

explanation.walkthrough: In British speech being made up means being delighted.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means fabricated, and also, informally in Britain, extremely pleased.

clue.text: Scenes 3-5 in version of Camouflage

indicators.note: in puts those letters inside the abbreviation

parts.note: VER is an abbreviation for version

indicators.note: 3-5 keeps only letters three to five of the word Scenes, dropping the rest

explanation.surface: Instructions to shoot scenes three to five of a war film about disguise.
explanation.definitionFit: A veneer is a thin surface layer that masks what lies beneath, so it disguises.

clue.text: Shoot again at alien found during search

indicators.note: found during places the alien inside the search word

parts.note: to rake is to search thoroughly, as in rake through
ET is the film alien

explanation.surface: A film crew reshoot after an extraterrestrial turns up in a hunt.
explanation.definitionFit: A retake is filming a scene once more, so the verb matches re-shooting.

clue.text: Ping pong fish bowls — a legitimate target?

definitions.meaning: tossing table-tennis balls into goldfish bowls is a classic fairground game
someone open to attack or criticism

explanation.walkthrough: The first half is read literally: a game played at a fair.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means someone who may justifiably be attacked, and literally a fairground amusement.

clue.text: Spooner's exercises set up on the reservation

indicators.note: Spooner swaps the opening sounds of the two parts

parts.note: PT, physical training, is exercises; its two letters are said as two syllables
PT, physical training, is exercises; its two letters are said as two syllables

explanation.surface: A clergyman leads workouts on a Native American reservation.
explanation.walkthrough: PT is said 'pee tee'; swapping the sounds gives 'tee pee'.
explanation.definitionFit: A tepee is a conical tent of Plains peoples, a dwelling erected on reservations.

clue.text: Separate from backward lad on Mediterranean island

indicators.note: backward says the name is read from right to left

parts.note: Sid is a typical boy's name, a lad
Crete is a Greek island in the Mediterranean

explanation.surface: Leaving behind a shy boy on a Greek island.
explanation.definitionFit: Discrete means distinct and individual, an adjective synonym of apart.

clue.text: Stop tree being uprooted from shadowy side street

indicators.note: shadowy suggests something vague and indistinct, so the remaining letters are reshuffled
uprooted means pulled out, so the word tree is taken out of the pool

explanation.surface: Halt a tree being dug up from a dim back lane.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being uprooted from' removes T, R, E, E from SIDE STREET, leaving SIDEST, which 'shadowy' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: To desist is to cease doing something, a synonym of stop as a verb.

clue.text: Hamilton's right out of place

parts.note: Hamilton is the setter, so Hamilton's is I am, shortened
proper means right or correct

explanation.surface: The setter claims to be correct but is out of order.
explanation.walkthrough: A setter's name with 's stands for I'm, the setter speaking.
explanation.definitionFit: Improper means unsuitable or inappropriate, so it describes something out of place.
